_comment: Edit this file to add or change a source. A source is only crawled when its access_rule is open_api or crawl_allowed, so changing a rule is a security decision and must carry its evidence in `basis`.

sources.name: India CSR
sources.basis: robots.txt disallows only /wp-admin/ and publishes a sitemap; read through the site's own WordPress REST API rather than by parsing pages.

sources.name: BRSR filings via NSE
sources.basis: robots.txt allows all but one test path. NSE blocks heavy bot traffic in practice and its terms were not read, so keep request rates low.

sources.name: North Eastern Council portals
sources.basis: robots.txt limits only core asset paths in the part read. Read the full file before a crawler runs against it.

sources.name: Assam CSR Policy 2019 and CSRAA
sources.basis: No robots.txt is served (404), so no crawl rules are declared, and the CSR policy documents are published for public use.

sources.name: Samhita reports
sources.basis: robots.txt allows everything except /admin/, /private/ and /api/. Terms of use were not read, so check them before production use.

sources.name: Dasra research and portfolio
sources.basis: robots.txt allows all paths. Used for landscape reports rather than entity records; terms of use were not read.

sources.name: India Philanthropy Report (Bain and Dasra)
sources.basis: robots.txt blocks only noindex, alumni, secure and mailing paths. The report itself is published for public download.

sources.name: CSR and funder official websites
sources.basis: A class of sites, not one host: each funder's robots.txt and terms must be read before that host is crawled. Sites cleared this way get their own entry.

sources.name: Annual Report on CSR Activities (Board's report annexure)
sources.basis: A public statutory filing published on each company's own site, so the rule is that company's robots.txt. Download politely, one host at a time.

sources.name: Board-approved CSR Annual Action Plan
sources.basis: A public board document published on each company's own site; the governing rule is that host's robots.txt, checked per site.

sources.name: CSR impact assessment reports
sources.basis: Published by funders on their own sites, so each host's robots.txt governs. These carry outcomes, baselines, geographies and partners.

sources.name: Company annual reports
sources.basis: Public statutory filings on each company's investor pages; the rule is that host's robots.txt. Carries the CSR chapter and the BRSR link.

sources.name: MCA CSR Data (MCA CDM)
sources.basis: robots.txt disallows automated access; the site also answers 503 outside India. Manual export from an Indian network, or Dataful's licensed mirror.

sources.name: Dynamic CSR Report export (MCA CDM)
sources.basis: Same host rule as MCA CSR Data: robots.txt disallows automated access. The Assam extract already held was scraped and should be re-pulled by manual export.

sources.name: CSR MIS reports (MCA CDM)
sources.basis: Same host rule as MCA CSR Data: robots.txt disallows automated access, and the portal answers 503 to requests from outside India.

sources.name: Give (funder and NGO profiles)
sources.basis: Give's terms bar data mining and limit content to non-commercial use. Manual entry with a source link stays allowed; a crawler needs Give's written permission.

sources.name: Dataful CSR Insights
sources.basis: robots.txt redirects rather than serving rules, so automated reading is not established. Treat it as a manual query surface over National CSR Portal data.

sources.name: National CSR Portal
sources.basis: The portal answers HTTP 403 to requests from outside India, including for robots.txt, so its rules are unknown from here. Manual lookup from an Indian network is allowed.

sources.name: Form CSR-2 project data
sources.basis: Reached through the National CSR Portal, which answers 403 outside India. Carries project spend, implementing agency and CSR-1 number when accessible.

sources.name: Prime Infobase CSR database
sources.basis: A commercial subscription product. Any use in Sangam needs a paid plan, and republishing its data in the open layer needs a written licence.

sources.name: Dataful CSR datasets
sources.basis: robots.txt allows /datasets, but downloads need a login and a paid plan, and republishing in the open layer needs a licence agreed with Dataful.

sources.name: CSRBOX
sources.basis: No robots.txt is served and no scraping clause was found, but the listings are the operator's curated product. Ask for permission or a feed before crawling.

sources.name: Free Resource Hub CSR Analytics
sources.basis: robots.txt blocks /api/ and /wp-content/, and the site states its contact data was scraped from elsewhere, so provenance is unclear. Cross-check only.

sources.name: FFRH funder datasets
sources.basis: Shared by FFRH for this project through Drive. Use follows the FFRH agreement, and funder-CSO links need CSO consent before any public display.

sources.name: SCALE funder dataset and tool assessment
sources.basis: Partner data from the SCALE collaboration, shared on request. Use only as the SCALE agreement allows; it carries funder data gathered from interviews.

sources.name: India CSR Navigator
sources.basis: Terms were not read and its data comes partly from Prime Infobase under licence, so Sangam reads it to learn shape rather than taking data from it.

sources.name: UNDP India research
sources.basis: Neither robots.txt nor terms of use have been read for this publisher. Manual reading is fine; check before anything automated touches it.

sources.name: BRSR filings via BSE
sources.basis: robots.txt returned no readable rules when checked, so whether it permits automated access is unknown. Carries the same filings as the NSE route.

sources.name: NITI Aayog Aspirational Districts and Champions of Change
sources.basis: robots.txt redirected rather than serving rules, so automated access is unestablished. The district list itself is published and can be downloaded by hand.
